_help: Ways to build real cybersecurity experience while job hunting. Shown in the tracker's Experience tab. Links are checked by the daily run; dead ones are flagged.

items.title: picoCTF
items.why: Beginner-friendly CTF by Carnegie Mellon; practice gym is open all year.

items.title: CTFtime event calendar
items.why: Find online CTFs to join this month; good placings are strong CV lines.

items.title: TryHackMe
items.why: Guided rooms for SOC analyst and pentesting paths; free tier available.

items.title: Hack The Box
items.why: Hands-on machines; the Academy has free modules.

items.title: OverTheWire wargames
items.why: Bandit teaches Linux/shell skills job ads keep asking for.

items.title: PortSwigger Web Security Academy
items.why: Free web security labs (OWASP Top 10) and Burp Suite practice.

items.title: HackerOne
items.why: Public programmes and vulnerability disclosure programmes; even one valid report counts.

items.title: Bugcrowd
items.why: Another large platform with beginner-friendly disclosure programmes.

items.title: Intigriti
items.why: Bug bounty platform with monthly challenges that teach real techniques.

items.title: ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity (CC)
items.why: Entry-level certification. The free exam programme ended in 2026, so it's now paid; the free Google/Cisco/Microsoft courses here are cheaper starting points.

items.title: Google Cybersecurity Certificate
items.why: Covers SIEM, Linux, SQL and Python for security; Coursera financial aid available.

items.title: Cisco Networking Academy
items.why: Free networking and cybersecurity courses; networking is the most common gap for cyber roles.

items.title: Microsoft SC-900
items.why: Security, compliance and identity fundamentals; free learning path.

items.title: CompTIA Security+
items.why: The best-known entry security certification (paid); good target for mid-2027.

items.title: Digital Talent Scholarship (Komdigi)
items.why: Government-funded digital and cybersecurity training for Indonesians; check open intakes.

items.title: OWASP Jakarta chapter
items.why: Local meetups: the fastest way to meet people who hire security interns in Jakarta.

items.title: Build a home SOC lab with Wazuh
items.why: Free SIEM/XDR; a write-up of a home lab shows the SIEM skills many SOC internships ask for.

items.title: Volunteer security check-ups
items.why: Offer a basic security check (passwords, MFA, backups) to a club, school or small business. Real experience that fits on a CV.
